questions.text: The average present age of ‘P’, ‘Q’, ‘R’ and ‘S’ is 17 years. The ratio of the age of ‘P’ after 2 years to the age of ‘Q’ 2 years ago from now is 2 : 1 respectively. The present age of ‘S’ is 4 years less than the present age of ‘P’. The present age of ‘R’ is equal to the present age of ‘Q’. Find the age of ‘R’ after 6 years from now.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Average present age of P, Q, R, S = 17 years

⇒ Total present age = 17 × 4 = 68 years

Ratio of (P’s age after 2 years) : (Q’s age 2 years ago) = 2 : 1

Present age of S = P − 4

Present age of R = Q

Formula used:

Average = Total ÷ Number

Ratio = Corresponding quantities

Calculations:

Let present age of P = x

Let present age of Q = y

⇒ Present age of R = y

⇒ Present age of S = x − 4

Total age equation:

⇒ x + y + y + (x − 4) = 68

⇒ 2x + 2y − 4 = 68

⇒ 2x + 2y = 72

⇒ x + y = 36 … (1)

Given ratio:

⇒ (x + 2) : (y − 2) = 2 : 1

⇒ x + 2 = 2(y − 2)

⇒ x + 2 = 2y − 4

⇒ x = 2y − 6 … (2)

Substitute (2) in (1):

⇒ (2y − 6) + y = 36

⇒ 3y − 6 = 36

⇒ 3y = 42

⇒ y = 14

⇒ Present age of R = 14 years

Age of R after 6 years:

⇒ 14 + 6 = 20 years

∴ The age of R after 6 years will be 20 years.

questions.text: 6 years hence from now, the average age of ‘T’, ‘U’ and ‘V’ will be 36 years. The ratio of the age of ‘T’ 4 years ago from now to the age of ‘V’ 10 years hence from now is 1 : 2, respectively. If the age of ‘U’ 5 years ago from now is 6 years more than the age of ‘V’ 5 years ago from now, then find the difference between the present age of ‘T’ and ‘U’.
questions.explanation:
Let the age of ‘T’ 4 years ago from now and the age of ‘V’ 10 years hence from now be x years and 2x years, respectively.

Or, the present age of ‘T’ = (x + 4) years

Or, the present age of ‘V’ = (2x − 10) years

Since the difference between the ages of two people remains constant,

So, the present age of ‘U’ = {(Age of ‘V’ 5 years ago) + 6 + 5}
= {(2x − 10 − 5) + 6 + 5} = (2x − 4) years

Sum of the age of ‘T’, ‘U’ and ‘V’
6 years hence from now = 36 × 3 = 108 years

So, the sum of the present age of ‘T’, ‘U’ and ‘V’ = 108 − (3 × 6) = 90 years

ATQ,

(x + 4) + (2x − 4) + (2x − 10) = 90

Or, 5x − 10 = 90

Or, 5x = 100

So, x = 20

Or, the present age of ‘T’ = (20 + 4) = 24 years

So, the present age of ‘U’ = (2 × 20 − 4) = 36 years

Therefore, required difference = 36 – 24 = 12 years

questions.text: There are four sisters Bhavna, Geeta, Simran and Sania. The age of Sania is (x – 5) years. The ratio of the age of Sania 5 years hence to the age of Geeta 2 years before is 5 : 4 . The ratio of the age of Bhavna 1 year before to the age of Sania 3 years hence is 1 : 4. Sania is 7 years older than Geeta, then find the age of Simran whose age is 1 year less than average age of other 3 sisters.
questions.explanation:
Given,

Present age of Sania = (x – 5) years

As, Sania is 7 years older than Geeta

Geeta’s age = (x - 5) - 7 = (x – 12) years

As, Ratio of the age of Sania 5 years hence to the age of Geeta 2 years before = 5 : 4

Therefore,

{ (x – 5) + 5 } / { (x - 12) - 2 } = 5 / 4

4 x { (x – 5) + 5 } = 5 x { (x - 12) - 2 }

4x = 5 ( x - 14)

4x = 5x - 70

x = 70

Thus,

Present age of Sania = 65 years

Present age of Geeta = 58 years

Let the age of Bhavna be B years

Ratio of age of Bhavna 1 year before to the age of Sania 3 years hence = 1 : 4

So,

(B – 1) / (65 + 3) = 1 / 4

4B – 4 = 68

B = 18

Bhavna’s age = 18 years

Average age of Sania, Geeta and Bhavna will be = ( 65 + 58 + 18 ) / 3

Average age of Sania, Geeta and Bhavna will be = 141 / 3 = 47

Given that age of Simran is 1 year less than average age of other sisters.

Hence, Simran’s age = 46 years.

questions.text: S is 4 years elder to R. Ratio of age of R after 24 years and age of S after 14 years will be 10 : 9. 3 years ago, sum of age of R and S was [x + 7] years. Find value of x?
questions.explanation:
Given:

S = R + 4

(R + 24) / (S + 14) = 10 / 9

3 years ago, R + S = x + 7

Formula used:

Substitute S in ratio equation and solve for R

Calculations:

⇒ (R + 24) / (R + 4 + 14) = 10 / 9

⇒ (R + 24) / (R + 18) = 10 / 9

⇒ 9(R + 24) = 10(R + 18)

⇒ 9R + 216 = 10R + 180

⇒ R = 36

⇒ S = 40

3 years ago: R = 33, S = 37

⇒ Sum = 33 + 37 = 70

⇒ x + 7 = 70 ⇒ x = 63

∴ The value of x = 63

questions.text: Six years ago, the age of Person A was 14 years less than 1.5 times his present age. The ratio of the age of Person B, 4 years hence to the age of Person C, 2 years ago is 2:1. Find the age of Person B, if the present age of Person C  is 50% more than the present age of Person A.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Six years ago, the age of Person A was 14 years less than 1.5 times his present age.

The ratio of the age of Person B, 4 years hence to the age of Person C, 2 years ago is 2:1.

The present age of Person C is 50% more than the present age of Person A.

Calculations:

Let the present age of Person A be x.

Six years ago, Person A's age = x - 6.

From the given condition: x - 6 = 1.5x - 14.

Simplify: 1.5x - x = 14 - 6.

0.5x = 8.

x = 16.

Present age of Person A = 16 years.

Present age of Person C = 50% more than Person A's age = 1.5 × 16 = 24 years.

Age of Person C, 2 years ago = 24 - 2 = 22 years.

Let the present age of Person B be y.

From the given condition: (y + 4) / 22 = 2 / 1.

y + 4 = 44.

y = 40.

The present age of Person B is 40 years.

questions.text: The average of the ages of A, B, and C 3 years from now will be 45 years. A's present age is 5/13 of the sum of ages of B and C. If the ratio of present ages of B and C is 7 : 6, then find the difference between the present ages of A and C.
questions.explanation:
Given:

(A + B + C)'s average after 3 years = 45 years

A's age = 5/13 of (B + C)'s age

B : C = 7 : 6

Formula Used:

Average = Sum of observations/Total number of observations

Calculation:

A.T.Q

(A + 3) + (B + 3) + (C + 3) = 45 × 3

⇒ A + B + C = 135 - 9 = 126 years

Also, A = 5/13 of (126 - A)

⇒ 13A = 5 × 126 - 5A

⇒ 18A = 5 × 126

⇒ A = 35 years

so, B + C = 126 - 35 = 91 years

Also, B + C = 7 + 6 = 13 ratio

∴ C's age = 91/13 × 6 = 42 years

Required difference = 42 - 35 = 7 years

∴ The required difference is 7 years.

questions.text: The ratio of ages of Aryan's grandfather and his father 14 years ago was 5 : 3. The present age of Aryan's grandfather is 7/2 of Aryan's age. If the age of Aryan 8 years ago was 16 years, then find the sum of present ages of all three.
questions.explanation:
GIVEN:

Grandfather : father (14 yrs ago) = 5 : 3

Grandfather = 7/2 × Aryan

Aryan's age = 16 + 8

EXPLANATION:

Aryan's present age = 24 yrs

Grandfather's age = 7/2 × 24 = 84 yrs

Grandfather's age 14 years ago = 70 yrs 

A.T.Q

70/(Father's age 14 yrs ago) = 5/3

5 ratio = 70 

3 ratio = 70/5 × 3 = 42 yrs

Father's present age = 42 + 14 = 56 yrs

∴ Sum of ages = 24 + 84 + 56 = 164 years

∴ The sum is 164 years.

questions.text: Eight years ago, Poorvi’s age was equal to the sum of the present ages of her one son and one daughter. Five years hence, the respective ratio between the ages of her daughter and her son that time will be 7 : 6. If Poorvi’s husband is 7 years elder to her and his present age is three times the present age of their son, what is the present age of the daughter?
questions.explanation:
Given:

Poorvi’s age = Sum of present age of her one son and one daughter.

Ratio of age of her daughter and son after 5 years = 7 : 6.

Poorvi’s husband is 7 years elder to her

Poorvi’s husband is 3 times the present age of their son.

Calculation:

Let present age of her son = x.

Present age of Poorvi’s husband = 3x

Present age of poorvi = 3x – 7

Eight years ago, Poorvi’s age = 3x – 15

Present age of her daughter = (3x – 15) – x = (2x – 15)

After 5 years, age of her daughter = (2x – 10)

Age of her son = ( x + 5)

⇒ (2x – 10) : (x + 5) = 7 : 6

⇒ 12x – 60 = 7x + 35

⇒ 5x = 95

⇒ x = 19

∴ present age of her daughter = (2x – 15) = 23 years.

questions.text: There are 25 members in a Lok-Sabha and the average of their ages is 28 years. The average age of the first 12 members is 26 years and the average age of the last 12 members is 28 years. If the age of Sachin is 5 years more than the age of 13th member, find the age of Sachin.
questions.explanation:
Given:

The total number of members in Lok-Sabha is 25.

The average of their ages is 28 years.

The average age of the first 12 members is 26 years.

The average age of the last 12 members is 28 years.

The age of Sachin is 5 years more than the age of 13th member.

Concept:

Often "average" refers to the arithmetic mean, the sum of the numbers divided by how many numbers are being averaged.

Formula used:

Total age = Average age × Total members

Average = Total sum of all numbers / Total numbers of items

Calculation:

Total members in Lok-Sabha is 25

The average of their ages is 28 years

Then, the total age of 25 members

⇒ Average age × Total members

⇒ 28 × 25 = 700 years

The average age of the first 12 members is 26 years

Then, the total age of the first 12 members

⇒ 26 × 12 = 312 years

The average age of the last 12 members is 28 years

Then, the total age of the last 12 members

⇒ 28 × 12 = 336 years

Now to find the age of 13th member

⇒ Total age of 25 members – (total age of first 12 members + total age of last 12 members)

⇒ 700 – (312 + 336)

⇒ 700 – 648 = 52 years

Thus, the age of the 13th member is 52 years.

We know that the age of Sachin is 5 years more than the age of 13th member

⇒ The age of 13th member + 5

⇒ 52 + 5 = 57 years

∴ the age of Sachin is 57 years.

Alternate Method

Alternate method:

The average ages of 25 members = 28 years

The average age of the last 12 members = 28 years

Than the average age of first 13 members = 28 years

We know that the age of Sachin is 5 years more than the age of 13th member

⇒ The age of 13th member + 5

⇒ 52 + 5 = 57 years

∴ the age of Sachin is 57 years.

questions.text: A family has 4 members. The sum of the age of father and son is 50 years. The ratio of the age of father and daughter 6 years back is 16 ∶ 5. The ratio of the age of mother and daughter 4 years later is 9 ∶ 5. Find the present age (in years) of the mother if the daughter is 4 years elder to the son.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Sum of the ages of father and son is 50

Calculations:

Let the present age of father and son be x and y respectively

⇒ x + y = 50     ----(i)

Let the present age of daughter be z

⇒ (x – 6) / (z – 6) = 16/5     ----(ii)

Age of daughter is 4 yrs more than that of son

⇒ z = y + 4     ----(iii)

Putting (iii) in (ii)

⇒ (x – 6) / (y – 2) = 16/5

⇒ 5x – 30 = 16y – 32

⇒ 5x – 16y = -2

Putting value of x from (i)

⇒ 5x – 16(50 – x) = -2

⇒ 5x – 800 + 16x = -2

⇒ 21x = 798

⇒ x = 38 yrs

Father’s present age is 38 yrs

⇒ Son’s present age = 50 – 38 = 12 yrs

⇒ Daughter’s present age = 12 + 4 = 16 yrs

The ratio of age of mother and daughter 4 years later is 9 ∶ 5.

Let the mother’s present age be M

⇒ (M + 4)/20 = 9/5

⇒ 5M + 20 = 180

⇒ 5M = 160

⇒ M = 32

∴ Present age of Mother is 32 years
